messages:
maya_product: Quick heads-up — I sketched a PRD draft for Structured Output + Tool Calling. Focus: schema contract, runtime validation, error handling, and launch gating. Asking for quick feedback on prioritization and acceptance criteria.

sam_engineering: posted the doc in drive -> https://redwood.app/drive/prd/so-toolcall-draft :eyes: will skim. main risk is runtime perf + extra validation latency.

vijay_ml: +1 on perf risk. We should quantify token-level validation cost. Also need fallbacks for quantized models with trimmed logits.

liz_design: UX question — when validation fails, should we surface structured errors to users or fall back to plain text? Customers care about determinism.

harry_cs: customer asks: finance app wants strict schema enforcement (no silent failures). Others prefer best-effort with helpful warnings. We should support both modes.

maya_product: proposal in PRD: two modes — strict (reject response, 400-ish error + structured diagnostics) and permissive (attempt repair heuristics and include validation metadata). Acceptance criteria below. @sam @vijay - can we implement both for MVP?

sam_engineering: we can ship permissive first (less latency). strict mode needs sync validation and a fail-fast path; could add as feature flag for Dedicated/Private first.

olga_security: note: strict mode must not leak sensitive fields in diagnostics. Diagnostics should be redacted and gated by config. Add that to compliance checklist.

maya_product: acceptance criteria (MVP permissive):
- server-side schema validation runs for 95% of requests within 50ms
- when validation fails, system emits a structured "validation" block with: error_code, confidence, repair_attempts, and the original raw text
- documented fallback: if repair_attempts == 0, client gets a clear non-200 response for strict mode; permissive returns repaired structure + trace
- E2E tests: 10 deterministic prompt sets covering missing fields, wrong types, extra items, nested array truncation

sam_engineering: engineering checklist:
- add lightweight JSON Schema subset validator (no $ref resolution in fast path)
- instrumentation: counters for failures, repair rate, validation latency
- config: per-route mode (strict|permissive|none), per-customer override
- rollout: canary on 10% traffic, sampling of failing payloads to S3 (PII redaction)

vijay_ml: edge cases to include in RFC tests:
1) truncated KV cache causing partial tokens -> incomplete JSON
2) hallucinated keys with valid types but semantically wrong values
3) streaming with mid-response validation failure -> how to cancel vs patch
4) tool call resolution failing (200 vs 500 from tool) -> structured error mapping

liz_design: for UX examples, add two sample flows: Payment parser (strict) and Summarizer (permissive). Include copy for error states.

harry_cs: we should add a launch criterion: 3 customers in beta with permissive mode on production and documented migration path for strict.

olga_security: also add KMS requirement for any sampled payloads; keep retention <30 days.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary deployment scheduled: 2026-06-15T02:30Z -> canary=10% -> rollback window 2h.

sam_engineering: next steps I suggest: 1) I will attach a perf microbenchmark by EOD (latency + p95) 2) @vijay will add validation cost numbers for top 3 models 3) @liz will draft error UX snippets 4) @maya will update PRD to include gating matrix

maya_product: thanks — I'll update the doc and open RFC in Monday's sync. If anyone has blocking concerns call them out here. Otherwise tagging this for prioritization in Q3 roadmap planning. :rocket:
